biology.dna-describe.0004.all: chromosomes are long DNA molecules (coiled with protein) in the nucleus; a gene is a section of DNA on a chromosome; a gene codes for a specific protein

biology.dna-describe-multi.0008.b: chromosome made of DNA; gene is section of DNA; codes for one protein

biology.dna-explain.0001.all: DNA is too large to leave the nucleus / stays in nucleus; mRNA carries copy of gene's code out through nuclear pore to ribosome where protein is made

biology.dna-explain-multi.0003.b: DNA cannot leave nucleus; mRNA carries copy of code to ribosome

biology.dna-mcq-rev.0004.all: A chain of amino acids folded into a specific shape

biology.dna-recall-multi.0003.a: DNA double-stranded, RNA single-stranded; DNA has thymine, RNA uracil; deoxyribose vs ribose

biology.environment-data-graph.0004.a: as height increases, mean number of limpets decreases
biology.environment-data-graph.0004.b: higher up shore exposed to air longer; more desiccation/temperature changes; less time submerged to feed / more predation by birds

biology.environment-data-pct.0001.b: tree canopy shades ground so less light; less photosynthesis; competition with tree roots for water and mineral ions

biology.environment-data-plot.0004.a: axes labelled, suitable scale, points plotted correctly, smooth curve
biology.environment-data-plot.0004.b: number of limpets decreases as height increases; decrease levels off near top

biology.environment-data-read.0003.c: exposed longer; desiccation; less feeding time / predation

biology.environment-explain.0001.all: canopy of tall trees absorbs most light; little light reaches floor; less photosynthesis so few plants survive; also competition for water/minerals

biology.environment-explain-multi.0002.b: transect samples systematically along a gradient; shows how distribution changes with distance/abiotic factor, random would miss the change

biology.environment-mcq.0002.all: placing quadrats at intervals along a transect

biology.environment-mcq-rev.0001.all: All the organisms of one species living in an area

biology.environment-prac-method.0003.all: mark out each area, use random coordinates (random number generator) to place quadrats; same size quadrat; count number of different species in each; many quadrats (e.g. 10) per area; calculate mean and compare

biology.environment-prac-plan.0001.all: C: compare sports field vs lawn; O: same species daisy, same time/season; R: random quadrats repeated e.g. 20 per area; M: count daisies per quadrat; S: same quadrat size, same weather/day; calculate mean per area and compare

biology.environment-prac-reliab.0002.a: to check results are repeatable / identify anomalies; calculate a mean so more reliable
biology.environment-prac-reliab.0002.b: light intensity / soil moisture / pH / trampling; measure with light meter etc. or do on same day; choose area with same conditions

biology.environment-prac-risk.0003.a: slippery rocks/incoming tide - wear grippy shoes / check tide times; or cuts - gloves
biology.environment-prac-risk.0003.b: use a quadrat with grid / identification key / count more quadrats

biology.environment-prac-step.0004.all: one transect may not be representative of whole field; repeating gives a mean and shows reliability/identifies anomalies

biology.environment-prac-vars.0002.b: percentage cover of the plant / number of plants
biology.environment-prac-vars.0002.c: quadrat size; same time/day; same person estimating; same interval

biology.environment-prac-plan.0001.problem: Mark scheme C point requires 'at least five values / a suitable range' and O point 'same biological material', which do not fit a two-site comparison of daisies (generic template).
biology.environment-prac-plan.0001.fix: C: compare two sites (sports field and lawn); O: same species of daisy identified; R: many random quadrats per site and mean; M: count daisies per quadrat; S: same quadrat size, same number of quadrats, same time of year.

biology.environment-prac-reliab.0002.problem: (b) Mark scheme examples (size of quadrat, water bath) are inappropriate for a field transect and omit the obvious answers (light intensity, soil moisture, pH, trampling).
biology.environment-prac-reliab.0002.fix: (b) e.g. light intensity / soil moisture / soil pH (1); measure it with a light meter/moisture meter/pH kit, or sample on the same day/in similar conditions (1).

biology.environment-prac-risk.0003.problem: (b) Mark scheme answer (precise apparatus, eye level, digital timer/sensor) is irrelevant to counting species per quadrat.
biology.environment-prac-risk.0003.fix: (b) use an identification key / a gridded quadrat / have the same person count / search the quadrat carefully, e.g. under seaweed (1).
